rice_brown_spot.name: Rice Brown Spot
rice_brown_spot.cause: It is caused by the fungus *Bipolaris oryzae* (also known as *Helminthosporium oryzae*).
symptoms: Small, circular to oval brown lesions on leaves with gray or whitish centers.
Lesions can enlarge and merge, leading to leaf drying.
Infected grains appear discolored and shriveled.
treatment: Spray fungicides such as Mancozeb or Carbendazim at recommended doses.
Remove and destroy infected plant debris.
Use resistant rice varieties when available.
prevention: Ensure proper field drainage to reduce humidity.
Use disease-free seeds and treat seeds with fungicide before sowing.
Maintain crop rotation to reduce fungal buildup.
rice_brown_spot.additional_info: Brown spot is often associated with nutrient deficiency (especially potassium) and stress conditions like drought.

rice_bacterial_blight.name: Rice Bacterial Blight
rice_bacterial_blight.cause: It is caused by the bacterium *Xanthomonas oryzae* pv. *oryzae*.
symptoms: Water-soaked streaks on leaf edges that turn yellow and then brown.
Leaves may wilt and die in severe cases.
When cut, bacterial ooze may appear from infected tissues.
treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides (like Copper oxychloride) to reduce spread.
Avoid using infected seeds and fields with history of blight.
Use resistant rice varieties such as IR20, IR64, and MTU 1010.
prevention: Use balanced fertilizer; avoid excess nitrogen.
Remove weeds and volunteer rice plants which can harbor bacteria.
Use proper water management to prevent spread through irrigation.
rice_bacterial_blight.additional_info: The disease spreads quickly under warm, humid, and rainy conditions and is one of the most destructive diseases of rice globally.

rose_black_spot.name: Rose Black Spot
rose_black_spot.cause: It is caused by the fungus *Diplocarpon rosae*.
symptoms: Circular black spots with fringed edges on upper leaf surfaces.
Yellowing of leaves around spots leading to premature leaf drop.
Reduced plant vigor and fewer flowers.
treatment: Prune and remove infected leaves and canes.
Spray fungicides such as Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Neem oil weekly during wet conditions.
Improve air circulation by proper spacing and pruning.
prevention: Water at the base of the plant to keep leaves dry.
Apply mulch to prevent fungal spores from splashing onto leaves.
Use resistant rose varieties if available.
rose_black_spot.additional_info: Black spot thrives in humid conditions and can severely weaken the rose plant if left untreated.

tomato_early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
tomato_early_blight.cause: It is caused by the fungus *Alternaria solani*.
symptoms: Dark concentric ring-shaped spots on lower leaves.
Yellowing and drying of affected leaves starting from the base.
Spots can also appear on stems and fruits, reducing yield.
treatment: Spray fungicides containing Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Copper oxychloride at regular intervals.
Remove and destroy infected plant debris.
Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness.
Provide good spacing between plants for air circulation.
Use certified disease-free seeds or seedlings.
tomato_early_blight.additional_info: Early blight occurs frequently in warm, humid climates and can cause major yield losses if not managed early.
